explanation: Under the continuous-partial-derivative criterion taught here, I and II qualify: their t derivatives are xe^{tx}sin(x) and −2tx²/(x²+t²)², both continuous on the stated domains. III fails this criterion because ∂|x−t|/∂t does not exist at x=t for 0<t<1. More general almost-everywhere differentiation results can handle III, but the lesson's stated criterion cannot.
